messages:
Marina Chen: Quick follow-up to the active/active RFC — I want to capture a tiny, implementable safe path for session routing + writes that we can ship to staging this quarter. Main constraints: data residency tags, avoid global coord, graceful read/write fallbacks.

Devin R.: +1. Can you sketch the minimal client+proxy changes?

Marina Chen: Idea: each tenant gets a pinned write-region (derived from residency tag or SLA). Client includes X-Write-Region hint and X-Prefer-Local boolean. Proxy uses hint for routing; if write-region is unavailable it tries a tiered fallback (reserved-dedicated -> nearest-fallback-region -> reject). Reads default to nearest region with eventual update of KV caches.

Sachin Patel: That aligns with what ops can support. Two quick risks: 1) write conflicts if tenant shifts primary, 2) cross-region audit logs for residency-sensitive customers.

Elaine: For (1) we should implement a simple monotonic generation number on the tenant manifest and require client to include current generation on write. If generation mismatch -> 409 + client refresh. Keeps it simple.

Tycho: Generation number looks good. Also proposal: add short-lived "write-token" that proxies issue to clients after successful write-region lease. Token TTL 30s, rotated on region move. Helps avoid global consensus.

Marina Chen: Nice. That solves fast-fail on split-brain scenarios. For audit logs, Sachin, can you confirm whether we can stream per-tenant logs to a residency bucket per region? Ops-bot: will correlate on tenant_id and region tag.

ops-bot: Canary pipeline triggered: policy/session-routing-v1 applied to staging clusters in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Logs will be forwarded to staging-residency-buckets.

Devin R.: Implementation notes for the proxy: lightweight state machine: LOOKUP -> ROUTE_WRITE -> VERIFY_TOKEN -> FORWARD. If VERIFY_TOKEN fails, return 409 + body: "stale-generation: please refresh manifest". Keep retries client-side with exponential backoff.

Marina Chen: Sample routing policy (for the config repo):
```json
{
  "routing": "primary-per-tenant",
  "fallbacks": ["reserved-dedicated","nearest-compatible","reject"],
  "client_hints": ["X-Write-Region","X-Prefer-Local","X-Manifest-Gen"]
}
```

Sachin Patel: Ops caveat: make sure the fallback list is order-sensitive and that reserved-dedicated respects residency constraints (no cross-border writes for GDPR customers). We'll add a residency check step before fallback attempts.

Tycho: I'll prototype a client SDK change that sets X-Manifest-Gen from local cached manifest and auto-refreshes on 409. ETA EOW for a PoC.

Elaine: I'll add the manifest generation and write-token logic into the tenancy service. Minimal API: GET /tenants/:id/manifest, POST /tenants/:id/lease (returns token).

Marina Chen: Action items: 1) Tycho prototype client SDK (PoC by EOW), 2) Elaine add manifest/gen + lease endpoints (PR next week), 3) Sachin ops: residency-aware fallback enforcement and logging, 4) Devin: small proxy state machine + 409 semantics. We'll run the staging canary and exercise a simulated region outage.

Devin R.: On the simulated outage: remember to test KV cache eviction semantics. We should avoid stale prefetched prefixes causing silent read-after-write anomalies. Add a short TTL on prefetched cache for tenants under migration.

Marina Chen: Good call — add caching TTL override when manifest.gen increments. Ok team — tagging this as follow-up work for the RFC. Ping me if blockers pop up. :thumbsup:
